cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the not-knowing has not closed you down.
cells.ask: Tell one person about a plan you haven't finished forming, and leave it open when they ask how it will work.
cells.core: You can stand in the middle of uncertainty without forcing it to resolve. Something is being felt forward, a shape you sense before you can name it, and instead of demanding the whole picture you stay with the next step and let the road show its next turn. That is not passivity. It is contact with what is coming. Keeping this costs you the ache of not yet. Not every week offers a signal that confirms you are on the right track, and the openness only holds while real engagement is feeding it. When direction comes from genuine feeling you can carry ambiguity for a long time. When it comes from habit, the same openness starts to feel like fog. To grow from here, tend one thing long enough to see it through, because sustained care is what makes a vision hold.
cells.sheetLine: You can carry not-knowing without forcing the answer.
cells.verb: Opening to what is not yet clear with first-time wonder
cells.place: In the middle of a road that only shows one step at a time

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future that hasn't been given to you yet.
cells.ask: Pick one unfinished thing and do the smallest concrete step today, without checking whether the whole thing makes sense first.
cells.core: You are running ahead of what is actually here. Your imagination has gotten out in front of your experience, and instead of letting feeling catch up, you keep projecting what might happen and trying to control it before it arrives. That is not foolishness. It is a live gift working overtime. But when the vision runs ahead of what has been digested, it stops being sight and starts being strain. The fix is not to stop imagining. It is to give the imagining something material to rest on. Small, real, everyday structure is what keeps the fire from burning your own hands. If you keep forcing clarity before it is ready, you will tire out the very sensitivity that makes you good at this. If you can slow down and let one thing grow at its own speed, the vision returns with more substance and less noise.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that closed behind you and calling it a wall ahead.
cells.ask: Name one assumption you're carrying about how something will go, then ask someone who knows you whether it still fits.
cells.core: The gift is still there, but it has gone quiet. You used to be able to walk into the unknown with a kind of trust, and now you wait for certainty before you move, and since certainty does not come, you stay put. That is not a failure of imagination. It is imagination that has been starved of new information. The way back is not to force yourself to feel open. It is to let something small confirm your perception again. Let a quiet impression land and check whether it was right. Let someone else's view meet yours without argument. Wonder does not come back by demand. It comes back when your own read proves accurate enough to be trusted. You do not need the whole road. You need one true thing to stand on, and then the next.

cells.tense: You are already writing the next step and calling it someone else's hand.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to yourself or someone else, that one thing you keep calling the situation is actually your read on it.
cells.core: You are already navigating. You sense the shape before it is said. You move through the unclear space with a steadiness you do not give yourself credit for. It gets described as if the clarity were coming from outside you, from the timing, from the circumstances, from what other people are doing. The steering is running. What is missing is admitting it out loud. That matters, because a read nobody owns cannot be refined. It can only wait for something else to confirm it. The way back is not more imagination. It is simpler, more embodied practice: notice one thing you see clearly, write it down, and let that be enough evidence that you are the one who saw it. You are not a passenger in this. You are holding the pen.
